Concepts

The three building blocks every Godzilla pipeline is made of.

Start with Pipelines

Godzilla is built from three ideas that compose into everything else in these docs. Understanding how they relate makes the rest of the platform — guides, API reference, SDKs — much easier to follow.

Concept

Pipelines

Named, versioned workflows that move data from a source to a destination through optional transforms.

 Concept

Connectors

Pre-built integrations to external systems — sources, destinations, or both.

 Concept

Events

The atomic unit of data flowing through a pipeline, plus the platform's own lifecycle events.

 Concept

Schemas

How event payload shapes are declared and validated using JSON Schema.

How they fit together

A pipeline reads events from a source connector, transforms them, and writes them to a destination connector. You can assign schemas to validate that events match your expected data structure before processing. Everything else in Godzilla — retries, webhooks, monitoring — is built on top of that single loop.

Definitions

Short definitions for every term used throughout these docs.

Pipeline
A named, versioned workflow that moves data from a source connector, through optional transforms, to a destination connector.
Connector
A pre-built integration to an external system — a source, a destination, or both.
Event
The atomic unit of data moving through a pipeline, or a platform lifecycle notification like pipeline.failed.
Webhook
An outbound HTTP request Godzilla sends to a URL you control when a subscribed event occurs.
Dead-letter queue
Where an event goes after exhausting its retries, rather than being dropped. See Handling errors & retries.
Cursor pagination
The pagination style used by every v2 list endpoint. See Limits, quotas & errors.
Workspace
The top-level account boundary an API key is scoped to.

# Godzilla Docs

> Everything you need to build data pipelines on the Godzilla platform.

## Pages
- [Authentication](https://localhost:3002/getting-started/authentication): Authenticate API requests with a bearer API key.
- [Changelog](https://localhost:3002/changelog): Recent changes to the Godzilla API and platform.
- [Concepts](https://localhost:3002/concepts): The three core building blocks of Godzilla: pipelines, connectors, and events.
- [Connectors](https://localhost:3002/concepts/connectors): What a connector is in Godzilla: a pre-built integration to a source or destination system, with its own auth and catalog of built-in types.
- [Events](https://localhost:3002/concepts/events): What an event is in Godzilla: the atomic unit of data moving through a pipeline, plus the platform's own lifecycle events.
- [Godzilla Docs](https://localhost:3002/index): Everything you need to build data pipelines on the Godzilla platform.
- [Installation](https://localhost:3002/getting-started/installation): Install the Godzilla SDK or start calling the REST API directly.
- [Pipelines](https://localhost:3002/concepts/pipelines): What a pipeline is in Godzilla: a named, versioned workflow that moves data from a source connector through transform steps to a destination.
- [Quotas & billing](https://localhost:3002/quotas-and-billing): Plan tiers, rate limits, and what happens when your account exceeds its quota.
- [Quickstart](https://localhost:3002/getting-started/quickstart): Go from zero to a running pipeline in five minutes.
- [Schemas](https://localhost:3002/concepts/schemas): How event payload shapes are declared and validated in Godzilla: schema definition, validation rules, and error handling.
- [Security & compliance overview](https://localhost:3002/security-and-compliance): How Godzilla handles data in transit and at rest, credential storage, and compliance posture.
- [Troubleshooting / FAQ](https://localhost:3002/troubleshooting): Common problems and fixes across pipelines, connectors, and webhooks. Also includes contact channels for technical support, sales, and security reports.

## api
- [API Reference](https://localhost:3002/api/index): The Godzilla v2 REST API: pipelines, connectors, events, webhooks, and limits.
- [Connectors endpoint](https://localhost:3002/api/connectors): Create, list, and rotate credentials for connectors via the v2 REST API.
- [Events endpoint](https://localhost:3002/api/events): Query and replay events that have flowed through a pipeline via the v2 REST API.
- [Pipelines endpoint](https://localhost:3002/api/pipelines): Create, list, and manage pipelines via the v2 REST API.
- [Limits, quotas & errors](https://localhost:3002/api/rate-limits-errors): Standard-tier limits, quotas, pagination envelope, and the v2 API's error response shape.
- [Webhooks endpoint](https://localhost:3002/api/webhooks): Subscribe to Godzilla platform lifecycle events over outbound HTTP via the v2 REST API.

## guides
- [Building your first pipeline](https://localhost:3002/guides/building-your-first-pipeline): Create a source connector, a destination connector, and the pipeline that connects them, end to end.
- [Connecting a data source](https://localhost:3002/guides/connecting-a-data-source): Choose the right connector type and authentication method for a new data source.
- [Guides](https://localhost:3002/guides/index): Task-oriented walkthroughs for building, connecting, and operating Godzilla pipelines.
- [Handling errors & retries](https://localhost:3002/guides/handling-errors-and-retries): How Godzilla retries failed events, when they're dead-lettered, and how to replay them.
- [Monitoring & alerts](https://localhost:3002/guides/monitoring-and-alerts): Watch pipeline health and get notified of failures via webhooks before they become incidents.
- [Scheduling & triggers](https://localhost:3002/guides/scheduling-and-triggers): Run a pipeline on a cron schedule or trigger it directly from incoming events.

## sdks
- [Node.js SDK](https://localhost:3002/sdks/node-js): Install and use @godzilla/sdk to manage pipelines and connectors from Node.js.
- [Python SDK](https://localhost:3002/sdks/python): Install and use godzilla-sdk to manage pipelines and connectors from Python.
- [SDKs](https://localhost:3002/sdks/index): Official Godzilla client libraries for Node.js and Python.
